content:
We have mass spec data: main peak at m/z 276.06655534899 (intensity 100). Likely molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually ESI positive gives protonated mass. So neutral mass ~275.058? Actually if m/z is protonated, M+H = 276.0666, so M = 275.0589 (subtract 1.007276). Let's compute: 276.066555 - 1.007276 = 275.059279. Approx formula? Use isotopic pattern: small M+1 peak at 277 with intensity ~16% (approx natural 13C abundance). 13C gives ~1.1% per carbon. 16% suggests about 14-15 carbons. Because 1.1% * nC ≈ 16% => nC ≈ 14.5. So maybe 14 carbons. Also M+2 peak at 278 intensity 33.6% which is high, maybe due to 2 13C or presence of Cl? But Cl gives M+2 ~33% of M. Indeed chlorine isotopic pattern: 35Cl (75.8%) and 37Cl (24.2%) gives M+2 ~32% of M. So presence of one chlorine atom would give M+2 ~32% and M+1 small. Here M+2 is 33.6% which matches chlorine. Also M+1 is 16% which is higher than typical for 13C alone (maybe due to 13C plus 37Cl? Actually chlorine gives M+2 not M+1). So likely one chlorine atom. So formula includes Cl.

Now compute exact mass: For chlorine, monoisotopic 35Cl mass = 34.968852. Protonated mass includes Cl-35. So neutral mass M = 275.059279. Let's try to guess formula with C, H, O, N maybe, plus Cl.

We can use DBE later. Let's approximate using typical atomic masses: C 12.0000, H 1.007825, O 15.994915, N 14.003074, Cl 34.968852.

Let’s try formula C14H?ClO? etc.

Let’s compute mass of C14Cl: 14*12 =168 + 34.968852 =202.968852. Need total 275.059279, remainder 72.090427. Could be O2 (31.98983) + H? Let's try O2: adds 31.98983 => 234.958682, remainder 40.100597. That's about 40 hydrogen (40*1.007825=40.313) slightly high. Maybe O3: adds 47.984745 => total 250.953597, remainder 24.105682 => about 24 H (24.1878) close. So C14H24O3Cl? Let's compute exact: C14 =168.0000, H24 =24*1.007825=24.1878, O3 =3*15.994915=47.984745, Cl =34.968852. Sum =168+24.1878+47.984745+34.968852=275.141397. Slightly high (0.082). Need 275.059279, lower by 0.082. Reduce H by maybe 1: H23 gives 23.170975, sum =274.133572? Wait recalc: 168+23.170975+47.984745+34.968852=274.124572. Too low. So maybe O2 and more H.

Try C14H22O2Cl: C14=168, H22=22.17215, O2=31.98983, Cl=34.968852 => total =256? Let's sum: 168+22.17215=190.17215; +31.98983=222.16198; +34.968852=257.130832. Too low.

We need 275.059. So maybe C15? Let's try C15Cl: 15*12=180 +34.968852=214.968852. Remainder 60.090427. O2 =31.98983 => remainder 28.100597 => about 28 H (28.2191) gives total 214.968852+31.98983+28.2191=275.177782 (0.1185 high). Reduce H to 27: 27*1.007825=27.211275 => total 214.968852+31.98983+27.211275=274.169957 (low). So maybe O3: 3*15.994915=47.984745 remainder 12.105682 => about 12 H (12.0939) gives total 214.968852+47.984745+12.0939=275.047497 close (difference -0.0118). That's good. So formula C15H12O3Cl? Wait H12? Let's compute: C15=180, H12=12.0939, O3=47.984745, Cl=34.968852 => sum =275.047497. Slight low by 0.0118. Could be within tolerance? Might need exact mass of protonated? Our target neutral mass 275.059279. Difference 0.0118 (approx 11.8 mDa). Could be due to rounding of masses. Maybe formula C15H13O3Cl? Add one H (1.007825) => 276.055322 (too high). So maybe C15H12O4Cl? Add O (15.994915) => 291.042412 too high.

Let's try C14H13ClO4? Compute: C14=168, H13=13.101725, O4=63.97966, Cl=34.968852 => total =279. (168+13.1017=181.1017; +63.97966=245.08136; +34.968852=280.050212) too high.

Maybe there is also nitrogen (adds 14.003074). Let's try C14H15ClN O2? Compute: C14=168, H15=15.117375, N=14.003074, O2=31.98983, Cl=34.968852 => sum =264. (168+15.117375=183.117375; +14.003074=197.120449; +31.98983=229.110279; +34.968852=264.079131) too low.

We need 275.059. Let's consider presence of Br? Br isotopic pattern M+2 ~ 100%? Not match.

Thus likely one chlorine.

Now we need to get SMILES. Could be a known compound with mass 276 (M+H). Maybe chlorobenzene derivatives? For example, 4-chlorobenzaldehyde (C7H5ClO) mass? C7=84, H5=5.039125, O=15.994915, Cl=34.968852 => total =140. (84+5.039=89.039; +15.995=105.034; +34.969=140.003) far lower.

Maybe chlorinated aromatic with some side chain.

Mass 276 suggests maybe C14H12Cl2? Two chlorines would give M+2 pattern double? But we only see one chlorine pattern.

C14H12Cl? Compute: C14=168, H12=12.0939, Cl=34.968852 => total =215.062752. Need 275, so need O? Add O3 (47.984745) => 263.0475. Add O4 (63.97966) => 279.0324 too high. So maybe C13H10ClO2? C13=156, H10=10.07825, O2=31.98983, Cl=34.968852 => total =233. (156+10.078=166.078; +31.99=198.068; +34.969=233.037) low.

Maybe C12H9ClO3? C12=144, H9=9.070425, O3=47.984745, Cl=34.968852 => total =236. (144+9.07=153.07; +47.985=201.055; +34.969=236.024) low.

Thus need more carbons.

C16H12ClO? C16=192, H12=12.0939, O=15.994915, Cl=34.968852 => total =255. (192+12.094=204.094; +15.995=220.089; +34.969=255.058) low.

C16H14ClO2? C16=192, H14=14.10955, O2=31.98983, Cl=34.968852 => total =273. (192+14.1095=206.1095; +31.9898=238.0993; +34.9689=273.0682) close to 275? Off by 2.

C16H16ClO3? Add O3 (47.984745) and H2 extra: C16=192, H16=16.1252, O3=47.984745, Cl=34.968852 => total =291. (192+16.125=208.125; +47.985=256.11; +34.969=291.079) too high.

C15H14ClO2? C15=180, H14=14.10955, O2=31.98983, Cl=34.968852 => total =261. (180+14.1095=194.1095; +31.9898=226.0993; +34.9689=261.0682) low.

C15H16ClO3? C15=180, H16=16.1252, O3=47.984745, Cl=34.968852 => total =279. (180+16.125=196.125; +47.985=244.11; +34.969=279.079) high.

C15H13ClO3? H13=13.101725 => total =275. (180+13.1017=193.1017; +47.9847=241.0864; +34.9689=276.0553) that's 276.0553 (neutral). Wait compute: 180+13.1017=193.1017; +47.9847=241.0864; +34.9689=276.0553. That's 276.0553, which is 1.0 higher than target 275.059. So maybe our target neutral mass is off because maybe the observed m/z is the molecular ion (M+?) Could be [M+Na]+? Sodium adduct adds 22.989218. If m/z 276 is [M+Na]+, then neutral M = 276 - 22.989 = 253.07. That seems less likely given isotopic pattern of chlorine still present? Sodium adduct would still show chlorine pattern. Let's test: M = 276.0666 - 22.989218 = 253.0773. Then formula maybe C14H13ClO? Compute: C14=168, H13=13.1017, O=15.9949, Cl=34.9689 => total =232. (168+13.1017=181.1017; +15.9949=197.0966; +34.9689=232.0655) low.

C15H13Cl? C15=180, H13=13.1017, Cl=34.9689 => total =228.07 low.

Thus likely protonated.

Our best candidate C15H13ClO3 gave neutral 276.0553, which is 0.996 higher than target 275.059. Wait we mis-subtract? Let's recompute target neutral mass precisely: Observed m/z 276.066555 (assuming [M+H]+). Subtract proton mass 1.007276 = 275.059279. Good.

Our candidate neutral 276.0553 is 0.996 higher, not close.

Maybe the observed is [M+Na]+? Then neutral 276.0666 - 22.989218 = 253.0773. Let's try formula C13H13ClO2? C13=156, H13=13.1017, O2=31.9898, Cl=34.9689 => total =236. (156+13.1017=169.1017; +31.9898=201.0915; +34.9689=236.0604) low.

C14H13ClO2? C14=168, H13=13.1017, O2=31.9898, Cl=34.9689 => total =247. (168+13.1017=181.1017; +31.9898=213.0915; +34.9689=248.0604) close to 253? still low.

C15H13ClO2? C15=180, H13=13.1017, O2=31.9898, Cl=34.9689 => total =260. (180+13.1017=193.1017; +31.9898=225.0915; +34.9689=260.0604) still low.

C16H13ClO2? C16=192, H13=13.1017, O2=31.9898, Cl=34.9689 => total =272. (192+13.1017=205.1017; +31.9898=237.0915; +34.9689=272.0604) still low.

C16H13ClO3? add O3 (47.9847) => 288. (272.0604+15.9949=288.0553) high.

Thus maybe not sodium adduct.

Maybe the observed is [M+K]+ (38.963707). Then neutral = 276.0666 - 38.9637 = 237.1029. Could match C14H13Cl? C14+Cl = 202.969, need 34 more -> maybe O2? Add O2 31.99 => 234.96, close.

But isotopic pattern of chlorine still present.

Given limited time, perhaps we can search NMR to get structure. Let's get proton NMR.
